sources.citation: Whitney, W. D. (1889). A Sanskrit Grammar, including both the Classical Language, and the Older Dialects, of Veda and Brāhmaṇa. 2nd ed. Leipzig: Breitkopf & Härtel; Boston: Ginn. (Section numbering unchanged in the 1896 issue used for searching.)
sources.used_for: Standard descriptive grammar in English for both Classical and Vedic: sounds, sandhi (§§100–260), guṇa and vṛddhi (§§235–240), declension (§§261–526), conjugation (§§527–1073), compounds (§§1246–1316). Section numbers cited in lessons.
sources.access: Public domain. Wikisource text (validated, 1889 edition) opened; full-text search done on the archive.org OCR of the 1896 issue (identifier whitney-a-sanskrit-grammar), whose OCR garbles Devanagari and diacritics: read forms from Wikisource or a page scan, never from the OCR.

sources.citation: Macdonell, A. A. (1927). A Sanskrit Grammar for Students. 3rd ed. London: Oxford University Press.
sources.used_for: Compact Classical grammar with a syntax chapter (ch. VII) and appendices on verbs, metre and Vedic. Second check of paradigms; pronunciation notes (§15); table of contents used to check the syllabus.
sources.access: Public domain (author d. 1930; published 1927). archive.org scan and OCR opened; OCR is poor for Devanagari.

sources.citation: Macdonell, A. A. (1916). A Vedic Grammar for Students. Oxford: Clarendon Press.
sources.used_for: Vedic forms and accent for san-07-10 only.
sources.access: Public domain. archive.org text opened (downloaded and searched).

sources.citation: Macdonell, A. A. (1910). Vedic Grammar. Grundriss der indo-arischen Philologie und Altertumskunde I.4. Strassburg: Trübner.
sources.used_for: Fuller Vedic reference behind macdonell1916.
sources.access: Public domain. archive.org landing page opened; text not read in this session.

sources.citation: Perry, E. D. (1885). A Sanskrit Primer, based on the Leitfaden für den Elementarcursus des Sanskrit of Georg Bühler. New York: Columbia College. (Scan of a later printing.)
sources.used_for: Teaching order of a classic primer (present class 1 and visarga rule in lesson I); graded exercises as models.
sources.access: Public domain. archive.org text opened.

sources.citation: Lanman, C. R. (1884). A Sanskrit Reader, with Vocabulary and Notes. Boston: Ginn. (1912 printing scanned.)
sources.used_for: Traditional first reader beginning with Nala; notes useful for part 8.
sources.access: Public domain. archive.org landing page opened; text not read in this session.

sources.citation: Speijer, J. S. (1886). Sanskrit Syntax. Leiden: Brill.
sources.used_for: Classical syntax with cited examples: cases, participles, absolutes, relative clauses, iti, moods. Main syntax authority for parts 5 and 6.
sources.access: Public domain. archive.org text opened and searched (absolute locative and genitive §§365–370; cases ch. III–VIII; compounds ch. X).

sources.citation: Monier-Williams, M. (1899). A Sanskrit-English Dictionary. New ed. Oxford: Clarendon Press. Digital edition: Cologne Digital Sanskrit Dictionaries.
sources.used_for: Meanings, root classes and attested forms (with text references) for every headword.
sources.access: Public domain; open online. Search opened and a lookup (gam) tested in this session.

sources.citation: Apte, V. S. (1890). The Practical Sanskrit-English Dictionary. Poona. Digital edition: Cologne Digital Sanskrit Dictionaries (AP90).
sources.used_for: Classical usage and meanings, with citations from Kālidāsa and the śāstras; second dictionary.
sources.access: Public domain; open online. Search page opened.

sources.citation: Wiktionary, the free dictionary (English edition): Sanskrit entries with declension and conjugation tables.
sources.used_for: Checking individual inflected forms. Tables print Vedic accents and Vedic-only variants (footnoted); strip accents and ignore footnoted Vedic forms for Classical.
sources.access: Open (CC BY-SA). Queried with tools/wikt.py in Devanagari (e.g. python3 tools/wikt.py देव Sanskrit).

sources.citation: Huet, G. The Sanskrit Heritage Site (declension, conjugation and sandhi engines; Heritage dictionary). INRIA Paris.
sources.used_for: Second mechanical check of paradigms and of sandhi; segmenter for attested lines.
sources.access: Open online. Landing and dictionary pages opened; the engines were not run in this session.

sources.citation: GRETIL: Göttingen Register of Electronic Texts in Indian Languages. SUB Göttingen.
sources.used_for: Texts for attested examples and part 8: Mahābhārata (BORI critical edition e-text, incl. Bhagavad Gītā = MBh 6.23–40 and Nala = MBh 3.50–78), Rāmāyaṇa (critical edition), Hitopadeśa, Kālidāsa, Manusmṛti, Pañcatantra.
sources.access: Open online. Files opened and searched in this session: Bhagavadgītā (bhgce__u.htm), MBh 3 (mbh_03_u.htm), Hitopadeśa, Rāmāyaṇa, Raghuvaṃśa, Manusmṛti, Pañcatantra. E-texts carry their own terms (BORI e-text (C) 1999; many files CC BY-NC-SA): quote short passages with citation, do not bundle whole files.

sources.citation: Sukthankar, V. S. et al., eds. (1933–1966). The Mahābhārata, critically edited. Poona: Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute.
sources.used_for: Edition behind the GRETIL Mahābhārata and Gītā texts; verse numbers cited follow it.
sources.access: Consulted only through the GRETIL e-text.

sources.citation: Bhatt, G. H., Shah, U. P. et al., eds. (1960–1975). The Vālmīki-Rāmāyaṇa, critical edition. Baroda: Oriental Institute.
sources.used_for: Edition behind the GRETIL Rāmāyaṇa text (John Smith's e-text); verse numbers cited follow it.

sources.citation: Hellwig, O. (2010–). DCS: The Digital Corpus of Sanskrit.
sources.used_for: Sandhi-split, lemmatised corpus: frequencies for choosing vocabulary, and checking how a line splits.
